extraction_metadata.notes: Reverse-engineered from arXiv:2602.00019 (Ge et al., Feb 2026). Four-component agentic protein binder design framework.

title: AutoBinder Agent: An MCP-Based Agent for End-to-End Protein Binder Design
subtitle_or_tagline: LLM + Model Context Protocol coordinating MaSIF + Rosetta + ProteinMPNN + AlphaFold3
topic: An agentic drug-design framework that uses a Large Language Model together with the Model Context Protocol to coordinate heterogeneous biochemical databases, modular toolchains, and task-specific AI models for end-to-end protein binder generation. Starting from a target structure, the system performs surface analysis, scaffold grafting, pose construction, sequence optimization, and structure prediction in a single protocol-driven workflow.

components.name: LLM Coordinator
components.role: Plans and orchestrates tool invocations using Model Context Protocol

components.name: MaSIF (site + seed-search)
components.role: Geometric deep learning for protein-protein interaction site identification

components.name: Rosetta
components.role: Grafts protein fragments onto backbones to form mini-protein scaffolds

components.name: ProteinMPNN
components.role: Redesigns amino-acid sequences for the grafted scaffolds

components.name: AlphaFold3
components.role: Predicts complex structures at near-experimental accuracy

architecture.data_flow: Target structure -> MaSIF site/seed search -> Rosetta scaffold grafting + pose construction -> ProteinMPNN sequence redesign -> AlphaFold3 structure prediction -> designed binder

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Identify PPI site on target surface (MaSIF-site).
Step 2 - Search for seed geometries matching the site (MaSIF-seed-search).
Step 3 - Graft mini-protein scaffold around seed (Rosetta).
Step 4 - Redesign sequence for stability and affinity (ProteinMPNN).
Step 6 - Iterate or accept based on predicted interface quality.
key_claims: Protocol-driven LLM coordination replaces rigid script-based workflows for drug design.
Integrates four state-of-the-art components (MaSIF, Rosetta, ProteinMPNN, AlphaFold3) under a single MCP-based agent.
Improves reproducibility, extensibility, portability, and auditability across the binder-design process.
Reduces manual overhead compared to stitching tools by hand.
caveats_or_warnings: The framework orchestrates existing tools; it does not itself introduce a new geometric or thermodynamic bound on binding.
Auditability here is protocol-level (which tool ran when), not mathematical (no per-step displacement bound).
MCP is still emerging as a standard; ecosystem maturity may constrain reproducibility in practice.
